BiblicalUsage: Sepharvaim was a city in Syria that the king of Assyria conquered, and its people were settled in Samaria after Israel was carried away. The Sepharvites brought their gods with them, and burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech. When the Assyrian envoys mocked Jerusalem, they named the gods of Sepharvaim among the gods that had failed to save their cities.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Sepharvaim shows what exile does — a people carried off, and their gods carried with them, and neither one able to save.
